items.prompt: What is a joint?

options.why: Muscles pull on bones. A joint is where bones meet.

options.text: a place where two bones meet

options.why: The skull is made of bones. A joint is where bones meet.
Muscles end in tendons. A joint is where bones meet.

hints: Bend your elbow and your knee.
Something lets your skeleton bend at these places.
What meets at your elbow?
items.explanation: A joint is a place where two bones meet. Joints let the skeleton bend and move.

items.prompt: Muscles can only do one thing to a bone. What is it?

options.why: Muscles cannot push. They can only pull.

options.text: twist it into a new shape
options.why: Muscles move bones. They do not change their shape.
Muscles do not make bones longer.

hints: When a muscle works, it gets shorter.
Think about what a shortening muscle does to the bone it is joined to.
Imagine a rope tied to a door being made shorter.
items.explanation: A muscle gets shorter, or contracts, and pulls on a bone. Muscles cannot push.

items.prompt: Match each joint to how it moves.
hints: Try moving each joint in your own body.
A door hinge only opens one way.
Which joint can swing your arm in a full circle?
items.explanation: The elbow is a hinge joint that bends one way. The shoulder is a ball-and-socket joint that moves all around, and the skull bones are joined by fixed joints.

items.prompt: You bend your arm at the elbow. What does your biceps muscle do?

options.why: That is what the triceps does. The biceps pulls.

options.text: It pushes the lower arm up.
options.why: Muscles cannot push. They pull.
Muscles do not turn into tendons.

hints: The biceps is on the front of your upper arm.
Feel it while you bend your arm.
Does it get harder and fatter, or softer and thinner?
items.explanation: The biceps contracts, getting shorter and fatter. It pulls the lower arm up, so the arm bends.

items.prompt: Put the steps in order to show how you bend your arm.
items: Your brain sends a message to your biceps.
The biceps contracts and gets shorter.
The biceps pulls on a bone in your lower arm.
Your arm bends at the elbow.
hints: Every movement starts with a message.
The muscle must get shorter before it can pull.
The bend happens last.
items.explanation: The brain sends a message, and the biceps contracts. It pulls on the lower arm bone, so the arm bends at the elbow.

items.prompt: Muscles work in ___: when one contracts, the other relaxes.
hints: Think about the biceps and the triceps.
There are two muscles working as a team.
The word you need starts with p.
items.explanation: Muscles work in pairs because each can only pull. One pulls a bone one way, and its partner pulls it back.

items.prompt: Choose 2 joints that work like a hinge.

options.why: The shoulder is a ball-and-socket joint. It moves in a circle.
The hip is a ball-and-socket joint too.
Skull bones are joined by fixed joints that do not move.

hints: A hinge bends in one direction only.
Test each joint: can it swing in a circle?
Think about the middle of your arm and the middle of your leg.
items.explanation: Elbows and knees are hinge joints, which bend one way. Shoulders and hips are ball-and-socket joints.

items.prompt: What joins a muscle to a bone?

options.why: Ligaments join bone to bone at a joint.
Nerves carry messages. They do not join muscles to bones.
A joint is where two bones meet.

hints: It is a strong cord at the end of a muscle.
You can feel one at the back of your ankle.
Ligaments join bones to bones. What joins muscles to bones?
items.explanation: Tendons are strong cords that join muscles to bones. When a muscle contracts, its tendon pulls the bone.

items.prompt: Your heart is a muscle. How is it different from the muscles in your arm?

options.why: The heart is not joined to bones. It pumps blood.

options.text: It works all the time without you thinking about it.
It only works when you exercise.
options.why: Your heart beats all the time, even when you sleep.
No muscle can push bones.

hints: Think about what your heart does while you sleep.
Can you choose to stop your heartbeat?
Arm muscles move when you decide to move.
items.explanation: The heart is a special muscle that pumps blood all the time. It works without you thinking, while you choose when to move your arm.

items.prompt: Your triceps muscle contracts. What happens to your arm?

options.why: The biceps bends the arm. The triceps does the opposite.
The triceps pulls the arm straight. It does not twist it.
When a muscle contracts, it pulls a bone.

hints: The triceps is on the back of your upper arm.
It is the partner of the biceps.
It does the opposite of the biceps.
items.explanation: The triceps is on the back of the upper arm. When it contracts, it pulls the arm straight.

items.prompt: A model arm has one string that pulls the lower arm up. Why can it bend the arm but not straighten it?

options.text: The string needs to push to straighten the arm.
options.why: Strings, like muscles, cannot push.

options.text: The joint in the model is fixed.
options.why: The arm can bend, so the joint is not fixed.
The string can pull. That is how the arm bends.

options.text: It needs a second string on the other side, like a muscle pair.

hints: The string works like a muscle.
A muscle can only pull in one direction.
How does your own arm get straight again?
items.explanation: A string, like a muscle, can only pull. To straighten the arm, a second string must pull from the other side, like the triceps.

items.prompt: Draw an arm bending at the elbow. Label the biceps, triceps, bones and elbow joint.

criteria.label: Draws upper and lower arm bones meeting at the elbow
Puts the biceps at the front and the triceps at the back

hints: Draw the bones first, meeting at the elbow.
The biceps is on the side that faces up when you curl your arm.
items.explanation: The upper and lower arm bones meet at the elbow joint. The biceps is on the front of the upper arm and the triceps is on the back.

items.prompt: Which of these is a joint?

options.why: The thigh bone is a bone. A joint is where two bones meet.
Skin covers the body. It is not where bones meet.
Hair is not part of the skeleton.

hints: A joint is a place where bones meet.
Look for a place where the leg bends.
Think about which part lets your leg bend.
items.explanation: The knee is where the thigh bone meets the shin bone, so it is a joint.

items.prompt: Muscles can only pull on bones. They can never ___ them.
hints: Think about what a muscle does when it contracts.
Use the opposite of pull.
It is a four letter word starting with p.
items.explanation: A muscle gets shorter and pulls. It cannot push a bone away.

items.prompt: The arm bends towards the right. Label the diagram.

figure.alt: Side view of an arm. A long bone goes down to a round yellow elbow joint, and a second bone goes out to the right. There is a muscle on each side of the upper bone. The arm is bending towards the right.

hints: The muscle on the inside of the bend is the biceps.
The muscle on the outside of the bend is the triceps.
The yellow circle is where two bones meet.
items.explanation: The biceps is on the inside of the bend and the triceps is on the outside. The elbow is the joint between the bones.

items.prompt: Tap the muscle that contracts to bend this arm towards the right.

figure.alt: Side view of an arm. A long bone goes down to a round yellow elbow joint, and a second bone goes out to the right. There is a muscle on each side of the upper bone. The arm is bending towards the right.

hints: The arm bends towards the right.
The muscle that bends the arm is on the inside of the bend.
This muscle is called the biceps.
items.explanation: To bend the arm, the biceps on the inside of the bend contracts and pulls the lower arm up.

items.prompt: Leo straightens his leg at the knee. The muscle at the back of his thigh relaxes. What must the muscle at the front do?

options.text: Contract and pull the lower leg straight

options.why: If both muscles relax, nothing pulls the bone, so the leg does not move.
Muscles cannot push. They can only pull.
Muscles stay muscles. They get shorter or longer.

hints: Muscles work in pairs.
One relaxes while the other does the opposite.
Remember what a muscle does when it moves a bone.
items.explanation: The pair works in opposite ways. The muscle at the front contracts and pulls the lower leg straight while the back muscle relaxes.

items.prompt: Maya squeezes a ball as fast as she can. She counts squeezes in the first and last 10 seconds. Fill in the gaps.
items.caption: Ball squeezes
head: Child
First 10 s
Last 10 s
Fewer squeezes
hints: Subtract the last count from the first count.
For Tom, work out 22 take away 15.
For Dewi, work out 25 take away 17.
items.explanation: Tom: 22 minus 15 is 7. Dewi: 25 minus 17 is 8. Tired muscles squeeze fewer times.

items.prompt: Putri tests if a heavier bag makes her arm tire sooner. Sort each item.

items.text: height the arm is held at

hints: Change is the one thing you alter on purpose.
Measure is what you record to see the result.
Everything else must stay the same to be fair.
items.explanation: She changes the mass of the bag and measures how long she can hold it. Everything else stays the same.

items.prompt: The chart shows how long Yuki held bags out at arm length. Predict the time for a 4 kg bag.

figure.alt: Bar chart of seconds an arm held a bag out. 1 kg: 58 seconds. 2 kg: 44 seconds. 3 kg: 31 seconds.

options.why: The time goes down as the bag gets heavier. 31 s is the time for 3 kg.
That is more than for 3 kg, but heavier bags tire the arm faster.
A heavier bag cannot be held for longer than a light one.

hints: Look at how the bars change from 1 kg to 3 kg.
Find how many seconds are lost each time.
Take that amount off the 3 kg time.
items.explanation: Each extra kilogram takes off about 13 seconds (58, 44, 31). So 4 kg would be about 18 seconds.

items.prompt: Choose 2 true sentences about muscles.

options.text: A muscle gets shorter when it contracts
Muscles push the bones into place
options.why: Muscles only pull. They cannot push.

options.text: Muscles work in pairs to move a bone both ways
A muscle is a type of bone
options.why: Muscles are soft and can change length. Bones are hard.

hints: Think about what a muscle does when it contracts.
Think about why we need two muscles at a joint.
Cross out any sentence that says push.
items.explanation: A muscle shortens when it contracts, and a pair lets a bone move in both directions.

items.prompt: Match each bone to the part of the body it protects.
hints: The skull is the hard case at the top.
Ribs make a cage around the chest.
The backbone runs down your back.
items.explanation: The skull guards the brain, the ribs guard the heart and lungs, and the backbone guards the nerves inside it.

items.prompt: Amara says, "My muscle pushes my bone up when I bend my arm." What should you tell her?

options.text: The biceps relaxes and pushes the bone up
options.why: A relaxed muscle is loose and does not move a bone. Muscles never push.

options.text: The elbow joint pushes the bone up by itself
options.why: A joint is only a meeting place for bones. It cannot make anything move.

options.text: Your skin pulls the bone up
options.why: Skin covers your arm. It does not move the bones.

options.text: The biceps contracts and pulls the bone up

hints: Muscles can do only one thing to a bone.
Think about the word contract.
Decide which direction the force goes.
items.explanation: A muscle works by pulling. When the biceps contracts it gets shorter and pulls the lower arm bone up.

items.prompt: Dewi tightens both her biceps and her triceps at the same time. What happens to her arm?

options.why: The triceps is also pulling the other way, so the arm cannot bend fully.

options.text: It stays stiff and hardly moves

options.why: The biceps is pulling too, so the arm cannot straighten fully.
An elbow is a hinge. It only moves forwards and back, and two equal pulls cancel out.

hints: The two muscles pull in opposite directions.
Think about a tug of war with two equal teams.
Which way does the bone move if both pull equally?
items.explanation: Both muscles pull the bone with similar force in opposite directions, so the bone stays almost still and the arm feels stiff.

items.prompt: To straighten your arm, the ___ contracts and the ___ relaxes.
hints: Remember which muscle bends the arm.
The muscle that bends the arm must now relax.
The triceps is on the back of the upper arm.
items.explanation: The triceps contracts to straighten the arm, while the biceps relaxes.

items.prompt: A robot model has 3 pairs of string muscles. How many strings does it have?
hints: A pair means two.
Count in 2s.
items.explanation: 3 pairs of 2 strings make 6 strings.

items.prompt: The shoulder is a ball and ___ joint, so the arm can move in many directions.
hints: A ball needs something to sit in.
It is a cup shaped hollow in a bone.
The word starts with the letter s.
items.explanation: In a ball and socket joint, the round end of one bone sits in a hollow in another bone.

items.prompt: True or false: Muscles pull on bones to make them move.
hints: What is joined to the bone?
Muscles can only do one kind of action.
Muscles pull, they do not push.
items.explanation: Muscles are joined to bones by tendons. When a muscle gets shorter, it pulls the bone and the body part moves.

items.prompt: True or false: Muscles push bones to move them.
hints: What does a muscle do when it contracts?
Can a muscle make itself longer by pushing?
Muscles only pull.
items.explanation: Muscles can only pull, by getting shorter. To move a bone back again, a second muscle pulls the other way.

items.prompt: True or false: Muscles work in pairs, so when one contracts the other relaxes.
hints: Think about bending and straightening your arm.
Two muscles are needed for two directions.
One shortens while the other relaxes.
items.explanation: In the arm, the biceps contracts to bend the elbow while the triceps relaxes. Then they swap to straighten it.

items.prompt: Muscles can only pull. They cannot ___.
hints: Think of the opposite of pull.
Pulling and ... are opposites.
It starts with p and has four letters.
items.explanation: Muscles can only pull, so they work in pairs to move bones.
